No, the intent no longer holds. The failed message was a transfer of the patient to WARD-B, bed BAY2-04, at 08:20 UTC. The bed-management system never applied it, and there is no receipt for it. The PAS then sent a later transfer to WARD-C, bed BAY1-07, at 08:45 UTC. The bed-management system applied that one, and its record now shows the patient admitted on WARD-C at version 2. So the 08:20 UTC message describes a bed the patient had already left.

Could a resend have done harm? Yes. Sending it now would move the patient back to WARD-B in the record, which would contradict the PAS's latest word on where they are. An earlier check held a resend back only because the 08:45 UTC transfer had not arrived yet. Now that it has, the right outcome is to send nothing.

The one alternative in the evidence (W1): if the bed-management system were set up to keep a full movement history, rather than just the patient's current place, the 08:20 UTC stop would matter as history. The case would then have gone to a person, to cancel the later transfer and replay both in order. That setting does not apply here. I can only answer questions; I cannot approve or resend anything.
